text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.87% today, reversing some of a steep two-week decline, as refining profits spiked across the sector. Global diesel prices surged following strikes on refineries in Russia and the Middle East tied to the Ukraine and Iran conflicts, which directly boosts margins for U.S. refiners like Marathon that turn crude into fuel products. The company is also running its refineries at 92.8% capacity, near full utilization, meaning it can capture more of those improved margins.

The stock's recovery today comes after a sharp drop of nearly 7% over the past two weeks—a period that included leadership changes at the company announced on October 29th. While today's move reflects sector tailwinds from geopolitical supply disruptions, the earlier decline suggests investors were digesting broader uncertainty around the company's direction and forward guidance.
